metadata.title: fix: Fix team join RBAC permissions
metadata.author: gcgoncalves

description: # 🐛 Bug-fix PR ## 📌 Summary Closes #3980 ## 🔁 Reproduction Steps 1. Login as an Admin user in the Admin UI 2. Create a public team 3. Create a non-admin user 4. Logout, then login as the new (non-admin) user 5. Request to create the public team ## 🐞 Root Cause The team permission check returned `[]` when `team_id` was out of token scope, incorrectly discarding global and personal roles needed for the join endpoint. ## 💡 Fix Description Changed the guard to skip adding out-of-scope team roles while preserving global and personal roles in the scope conditions. ## 🧪 Verification | Check | Command | Status | |---------------------------------------|----------------------|--------| | Lint suite | `make lint` | ✅ | | Unit tests | `make test` | ✅ | | Coverage ≥ 80 % | `make coverage` | ✅ | | Manual regression no longer fails | steps / screenshots | ✅ | ## ✅ Checklist - [X] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`) - [X] No secrets/credentials committed

reviews.author: vishu-bh
reviews.body:
LGTM 🚀  The change in `mcpgateway/services/permission_service.py` fixes the reported regression by preserving global and personal roles when team_id is out of token scope, which matches the join-request use case without reintroducing out-of-scope team-role access.

I also checked the new tests in `tests/unit/mcpgateway/services/test_permission_service.py `and `tests/unit/mcpgateway/services/test_permission_service_token_narrowing.py.` Coverage around token narrowing, public-only behavior, and cache-key isolation is strong, and the targeted test run passed locally. Nice fix and good regression coverage.

reviews.author: Lang-Akshay
reviews.body: This PR fixes a regression introduced by #3924 where _get_user_roles() returned [] early when team_id was outside the caller's token scope, inadvertently discarding global and personal roles (e.g. a platform-wide teams.join permission). The fix replaces the return [] with a conditional that skips injecting team-scoped SQL conditions while still querying global/personal roles. The change is surgical.

reviews.author: crivetimihai
reviews.body:
Nice fix, Gabriel — the root cause analysis is spot-on and the approach is clean.

## What the PR does well

- Correctly identifies that the early `return []` in `_get_user_roles()` was over-broad: it discarded global and personal roles along with out-of-scope team roles, breaking `teams.join` for users whose token didn't already include the target team.
- The fix is minimal and surgical — just restructures the guard into an if/else so team-scoped conditions are skipped while global/personal conditions are preserved.
- Good regression tests covering both the happy path (in-scope team includes team roles) and deny paths (out-of-scope team excludes team roles).

## Changes made during review

A few small additions on top of the original commits:

1. **Cleaned up stream-of-consciousness comments** in `test_get_user_roles_public_only_token_with_team_id_returns_global_personal_only` — replaced thinking-out-loud notes with a single clear comment.
2. **Added `test_explicit_team_id_excludes_out_of_scope_narrowed_token`** — query-level verification that the compiled SQL doesn't include out-of-scope team conditions for narrowed tokens (mirrors the existing public-only token test).
3. **Downgraded log from `warning` to `debug`** at the out-of-scope guard (line 519) — after this fix, every team join/leave by a non-member hits this branch as normal flow, so warning-level would be noisy in production.
4. **Fixed misleading comment** that said "should return empty list" right before asserting `len(roles) == 1`.
5. **Added `test_explicit_team_id_includes_team_roles_when_token_unrestricted`** — covers the `token_teams=None` + explicit `team_id` branch with query-level verification.
6. **Applied black formatting** to pre-existing violations in the token narrowing test file.

## Security review

- Team-scoped roles for out-of-scope teams are still excluded (invariant preserved).
- Consistent with existing behavior when `team_id=None` — global/personal roles were always returned.
- `check_permission()` still suppresses admin bypass for public-only tokens.
- No privilege escalation path identified.
- 104 permission service tests pass, 98% coverage on `permission_service.py` (3 uncovered lines are all pre-existing code outside this PR).
